page: Microsoft Azure FX48-24mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration built for workloads requiring constrained core counts coupled with extensive memory capacity. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs backed by 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. The underlying CPU supports broad vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AMX tile/int8 operations.

Hardware provisioning features an asymmetrical ratio of 1008.0 GB of system RAM, delivering 42.0 GB per vCPU. Storage includes 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, offering rapid temporary I/O without relying solely on remote volumes. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included, with GPU count sitting at zero. This constrained-core architecture offers a cost-effective operational profile for software environments licensed per core, maximizing usable memory without incurring excess licensing fees.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive per-core efficiency alongside stable multi-core capabilities. The instance attained a Geekbench single-core score of 2339.0 and a text processing score of 2938.0, placing both metrics within top-tier percentiles. Single-threaded gzip compression scored 34.71 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieved 14.24 GB/sec, ranking in the top 25%. Broader parallel benchmarks reflect its 24-vCPU ceiling, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 16414.0 and a PassMark CPU mark of 41633.42.

Given its massive memory allocation, strong single-threaded throughput, and local NVMe storage, the FX48-24mds_v2 is well-matched for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational database management systems with per-core licensing constraints, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
